title: Historical memory, register and critical source synthesis

questions.prompt: Complete the counterfactual: « Si le débat avait été public, davantage d'habitants ___ participé. »
choices: auraient
avaient
auront
questions.explanation: A past counterfactual uses plus-que-parfait with conditionnel passé: auraient participé.

questions.prompt: Choose the formal register for an evidence-based report.
choices: C'est carrément un truc de ouf.
Ça prouve tout, sans discussion.
Les résultats suggèrent une évolution notable.
questions.explanation: A cautious impersonal formulation suits a formal evidence-based report.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly introduces a hypothetical concession?
choices: Quand bien même cette mesure adopter, les obstacles disparaissaient.
Quand bien même cette mesure serait adoptée, des obstacles subsisteraient.
Quand bien même cette mesure est adoptée hier, des obstacles subsisteront hier.
questions.explanation: Quand bien même may introduce a hypothetical concession with conditional verb forms.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative construction: « Les auteurs ___ les travaux sont cités »
choices: dont
que
où
questions.explanation: Dont expresses the relation of whose works: les travaux des auteurs.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the passive voice correctly?
choices: La décision a contesté par plusieurs associations.
La décision était contester par les associations.
La décision a été contestée par plusieurs associations.
questions.explanation: The passive construction is auxiliary être plus past participle, here a été contestée.

questions.prompt: Choose the connector most appropriate for presenting a qualification.
choices: Par exemple,
Néanmoins,
Puisque
questions.explanation: Néanmoins introduces a reservation or counterpoint.

questions.prompt: Complete: « Il aurait fallu que les autorités ___ les résidents. »
choices: consultent
consulteront
consulter
questions.explanation: Il aurait fallu que calls for a subjunctive clause; consultent is the present subjunctive form.

questions.prompt: Which sentence distinguishes possibility from established fact?
choices: Les chiffres ont forcément été sous-estimés.
Il est certain sans preuve que les chiffres sont faux.
Il se pourrait que les chiffres aient été sous-estimés.
questions.explanation: Il se pourrait que introduces uncertainty with the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Which revision avoids an unsupported universal claim?
choices: Aucun contre-exemple n'existe dans le monde.
Dans les sources étudiées, plusieurs exemples vont dans ce sens.
Tous les peuples ont toujours agi de la même façon.
questions.explanation: Limiting the claim to the studied sources avoids unjustified universality.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le mémorial évoque certaines expériences de l'exil, sans prétendre représenter toutes les trajectoires. » What limitation is acknowledged?
choices: Its narratives are selective, not universally representative.
It includes every possible migration experience.
It rejects the existence of exile.
questions.explanation: The phrase sans prétendre représenter toutes les trajectoires acknowledges partial coverage.

questions.prompt: Read: « Selon l'archive municipale, le quartier a été réaménagé en 1978. » What is the claim's provenance?
choices: A contemporary eyewitness necessarily present.
An unspecified social media comment.
A municipal archive.
questions.explanation: Selon l'archive municipale identifies the cited institutional source.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'éditorial défend la réforme, tandis que l'enquête en documente des effets contradictoires. » How do the genres differ?
choices: The editorial has no viewpoint at all.
The editorial argues a position; the investigation reports mixed effects.
Both texts are neutral laboratory measurements.
questions.explanation: An éditorial advances an opinion, while enquête denotes investigation.

questions.prompt: Read: « Les témoignages ont été recueillis vingt ans après les faits. » What interpretive caution applies?
choices: Memory and later context may shape recollections.
Every recollection must be deliberately false.
No witness can remember any past event.
questions.explanation: A twenty-year interval is relevant to memory evaluation without discrediting all testimony.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le film juxtapose des archives sonores et des scènes reconstituées. » What should viewers distinguish?
choices: Two forms of identical primary-source footage.
All scenes as spontaneous recordings.
Documentary recordings from dramatized reconstruction.
questions.explanation: Reconstituted scenes are not identical to original archival recordings.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'étude corrige une première estimation après la découverte de nouveaux registres. » What does the revision show?
choices: The records had no relevance.
New primary evidence prompted a revised estimate.
The first estimate was guaranteed to be fraudulent.
questions.explanation: Newly discovered registers can legitimately change an earlier estimate.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le mot intégration possède des sens différents selon les acteurs interrogés. » What should an analyst avoid?
choices: Treating the word as having one uncontested meaning.
Identifying how speakers define the term.
Comparing how the term is used in context.
questions.explanation: Different actor definitions require careful contextual interpretation.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'article cite une loi, mais ne mentionne ni les décrets d'application ni les décisions judiciaires. » What is a source limitation?
choices: No law exists.
A statute alone automatically reveals every legal outcome.
The legal implementation and interpretation are not fully covered.
questions.explanation: Application decrees and court decisions may affect how a statute operates.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'auteur écrit “nous” sans préciser le groupe représenté. » What question is important?
choices: Why French has no plural pronouns.
Who is included or excluded by nous?
Whether nous is always first-person singular.
questions.explanation: The referent of collective nous affects representation and authority.

questions.prompt: You are analyzing a historical letter written by an official. What should you establish first?
choices: Its date, author, intended audience and institutional context.
Only whether its handwriting is attractive.
That its claims are automatically neutral.
questions.explanation: Provenance and audience help situate the purpose and perspective of the source.

questions.prompt: An essay compares two portrayals of migration. Which thesis is best bounded?
choices: Tous les récits migratoires sont identiques.
Un récit suffit à expliquer toutes les migrations.
Ces deux récits divergent surtout par la place accordée à la mémoire familiale.
questions.explanation: A bounded thesis identifies a specific contrast supported by the chosen texts.

questions.prompt: A source translated a politically charged term. What strengthens the analysis?
choices: Remove the term without comment.
Consult the original wording and explain the translation choice.
Assume one translation is always context-free.
questions.explanation: Translation choices may affect connotation and require transparency.

questions.prompt: You discover a claim quoted without its preceding paragraph. What is the sound next step?
choices: Read the surrounding passage before interpreting the quotation.
Treat the isolated phrase as the whole argument.
Discard all sources that include quotations.
questions.explanation: Surrounding context is needed to avoid a misleading isolated citation.

questions.prompt: A documentary mixes interviews and staged scenes. Which annotation is most precise?
choices: Présenter les reconstitutions comme des archives directes.
Dire que toute image filmée est une preuve indépendante.
Distinguer les témoignages filmés des reconstitutions narratives.
questions.explanation: Separating interviews and dramatizations preserves documentary evidence boundaries.

questions.prompt: An author writes a strong claim but the dataset covers just one region. Which revision fits?
choices: Les données rendent inutile toute réserve.
Dans la région étudiée, les données semblent appuyer cette hypothèse.
Dans le monde entier, le phénomène est prouvé.
questions.explanation: The limited region calls for explicit geographic and epistemic qualification.

questions.prompt: Two sources contradict each other about a policy's effects. Which strategy is strongest?
choices: Compare definitions, sampling, time periods and stated interests.
Select the newer source without reading it.
Average their claims without considering method.
questions.explanation: Method and context can explain apparent contradictions between sources.

questions.prompt: You want to acknowledge a persuasive counterargument. Which phrase fits?
choices: Toute objection est absurde.
Il est interdit de nuancer une thèse.
Cette objection mérite d'être examinée, bien qu'elle ne réfute pas entièrement la thèse.
questions.explanation: Acknowledging a challenge while evaluating its scope supports scholarly argument.

questions.prompt: A historical claim concerns a marginalized community. Which approach is responsible?
choices: Invent missing quotations to improve balance.
Include relevant community voices and identify archive gaps.
Treat the institutional archive as the only possible perspective.
questions.explanation: Source diversity and transparent archival limitations improve historical analysis.
